docs.title: Graph Drawing
docs.text:
Schematic drawings of graphs in Rhino, in Grasshopper, as SVG and as PDF.

Any graph whose nodes and edges carry a few styling attributes can be drawn: a sequence of actions, a program of interventions, the members of a structure and their connections. A drawing becomes SVG, PDF, Rhino geometry or a picture on the Grasshopper canvas.

The support graph of a timber corner structure, after Bruun et al. 2024: which member rests on which, wall by wall.

A drawing is made in three steps:

  1. A graph. A compas.datastructures.Graph whose nodes and edges carry styling attributes. frames makes one from a JSON of parts as boxes, from_model from a compas_model model, steps from a list of steps.
  2. A layout. layouts.support places the members of a frame in the manner of Bruun et al., layouts.layered puts the nodes of a directed graph in layers along its edges.
  3. A drawing. draw turns graph and positions into a Drawing: a list of plain items (circles, polygons, lines, text).
from graph_drawing import steps, layouts, draw

g = steps(["Release", "Lift the wall", "Withdraw post_3", "Insert a new post"])
pos, regions = layouts.layered(g)
drawing = draw(g, pos, regions, title="exchange of a post")

with open("steps.svg", "w") as f:
    f.write(drawing.to_svg())
drawing.to_pdf("steps.pdf")

See Drawing graphs and Rhino and Grasshopper.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: Graph Drawing needs Python 3.9 or newer and COMPAS 2.15.1 or newer. compas_model is needed only for from_model.

docs.title: User
docs.text:
Clone the repository and install it into your environment:

git clone https://github.com/augmentedfabricationlab/graph_drawing.git
pip install -e graph_drawing

With compas_model, for drawing models:

pip install -e graph_drawing[model]

docs.title: Rhino 8 and Grasshopper
docs.text:
Rhino 8 runs Python 3.9. Find its Python with

python -m compas_rhino.print_python_path

It looks like C:/Users/your_user_name/.rhinocode/py39-rh8/python.exe. Install the package there as well:

path/to/rhino/python -m pip install -e graph_drawing

Or open any Python 3 script in Rhino 8, go to Tools, Options in the script editor and add the src folder of the repository to the Python path. The Grasshopper component finds src on its own, see Rhino and Grasshopper.

docs.title: With a COMPAS scene
docs.text:
Importing graph_drawing.rhino registers scene objects for drawings, so a drawing can be added to a compas.scene.Scene like any COMPAS object:

from compas.scene import Scene
import graph_drawing.rhino  # registers the drawing for Rhino and Grasshopper
from graph_drawing import frames

scene = Scene()
obj = scene.add(frames.drawing(json_path), unit=0.2)
geometry = scene.draw()
colors = obj.colors  # one per piece of geometry, for a Custom Preview

In Grasshopper scene.draw() returns the geometry. In Rhino, outside Grasshopper, it adds the pieces to the document, each in its own colour. to_rhino(drawing, plane, unit) gives geometry and colours directly.

COMPAS looks for scene objects only in packages whose name starts with "compas", so importing graph_drawing.rhino registers them itself, after the COMPAS ones.

docs.title: The Grasshopper component
docs.text:
rhino/ in the repository holds a Grasshopper component built on the package. It reads a JSON of parts as boxes and shows the structure as boxes coloured by state, tags, the connections on the model, the support drawing next to the model and on the canvas below the component, a report, and a focus on one part with what it rests on and what rests on it.

  1. In Grasshopper add a Script component, double-click it, choose Python 3, paste rhino/stub.py and close the editor. Save the .gh file in the repository's rhino folder or next to it, so the stub finds rhino/component.py (or set the environment variable GRAPH_DRAWING_RHINO to that folder). If graph_drawing is not installed in Rhino's Python, the stub adds the repository's src folder to the path.
  2. Connect a File Path with data/timber_corner_structure.json to json_path once the inputs appear.

On the first run the component creates its inputs and outputs, places three Custom Preview components next to itself and wires them, then recomputes once. Edits to the package and to rhino/component.py take effect on the next recompute; rhino/gh_interact.py (the mouse callback, a .NET type) needs a Rhino restart.

Input json_path File Path to the JSON, the only required input show_geometric also show contacts the JSON does not list (default True) graph_origin lower left corner of the drawing in the XY plane (default: right of the model) graph_scale metres per drawing unit (default 0.2; a node has a radius of 0.3 units) show_on_canvas the drawing below the component (default True) canvas_width width of that drawing (default 900) export PDF and SVG into a Graph folder next to the .gh file select code or id of a part to focus on; takes effect when the value changes interactive clicks in the viewport and on the canvas drawing (default True) graph_style connections on the model: 0 joint (default), 1 liaison, 2 frame chain also mark the parts that lose all support from below once the selected one is out

Outputs: model, model_colors, model_tags, model_graph, model_graph_colors, diagram, diagram_colors, graph (COMPAS Graph of the contacts), support (COMPAS Graph, u → v means u rests on v), report, legend, pdf, svg, selected, affected, selection.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
steps makes a graph of labelled steps, as a chain or as any directed graph. layouts.layered puts the steps in layers along the edges and orders each layer so that edges cross as little as possible.

from graph_drawing import steps, layouts, draw

g = steps(
    {"r": "Release the joints", "p": "Prop the plate", "l": "Lift the wall",
     "w": "Withdraw post_3", "n": "Insert the new post", "s": "Secure"},
    edges=[("r", "l"), ("p", "l"), ("l", "w"), ("w", "n"), ("n", "s")],
)
pos, regions = layouts.layered(g)
drawing = draw(g, pos, regions, title="exchange of a post")

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
models.drawing draws a compas_model Model whose graph carries the state of an intervention, for example a state computed with Intervention Grammar. Members become boxes coloured by type, connections become arrows from the carried member to the carrying one. With positions, every member is drawn where it is in the structure:

from graph_drawing import models

# the middle of every member in the wall, in metres
where = {
    "sill": (1.5, 0.0), "plate": (1.5, 2.2),
    "post_1": (0.1, 1.1), "post_2": (1.5, 1.1), "post_3": (2.9, 1.3), "post_3.new": (2.9, 0.2),
    "rail_1": (0.8, 1.1), "rail_2": (2.2, 1.1),
    "brace_1": (0.4, 1.9), "brace_2": (2.2, 1.65),
}
positions = {name: (2.2 * x, 2.2 * y) for name, (x, y) in where.items()}
drawing = models.drawing(model, title="a wall after a prosthesis", positions=positions)

Without positions, the members are placed in layers along the arrows.

from_model gives the styled graph alone, for another layout. It reads these attributes:

On Attribute Values element nodes fabric "original", "new" (black ring) element nodes condition "sound", "damaged" (red) element nodes placement "in", "inserted", "out" (white, dashed), "missing" (yellow) element nodes type the role of the member, any name (colour) element nodes grounded True: an arrow to the ground node connections joint a joint description connections state "secured", "released" (dashed), "open" (dotted) connections at {element name: station} connections support (carried, carrier) or "both": the arrow

docs.title: Frames
docs.text:
frames.drawing reads the parts of a frame from JSON, as boxes with their dimensions and rotations and the connections each part lists, finds the contacts between the boxes and draws which part rests on which. The format is that of data/timber_corner_structure.json in the repository (schema 2.1.0). The drawing on the home page is this file:

from graph_drawing import frames

drawing = frames.drawing("data/timber_corner_structure.json")
drawing.to_pdf("corner.pdf")

frames.report lists what the JSON and the geometry disagree on, and frames.focus shows how every part relates to a selected one: what it rests on, what rests on it, and what loses all support from below once it is taken out.

docs.title: Reading a support drawing
docs.text:
• Every wall gets a region (dashed box), placed like a plan seen from above. Inside a region the members stand in columns from the outside in: ground, sills, posts, braces and struts, one column per rail height, top beams. Members of two walls stand between the two regions, members of no wall in the middle.
  • Codes: wall letter, type letter, number along the wall (FR3 is the front wall, rail 3), C corner. The black triangles are the ground.
  • Node colour is the member type, together with the type letter. Red ring: defective, yellow: missing, black ring: new.
  • An arrow points from the carried part to the carrying part, coloured like the carried part. Solid: listed by both parts, dashed: listed by one, dotted: touching but not listed, red: listed but not touching.

docs.title: Any graph
docs.text:
draw draws any compas.datastructures.Graph with positions for its nodes. It reads these attributes:

On Attributes nodes label, fill, stroke and stroke_width (a ring), text_color, label_size, bold, shape ("circle", "octagon", "box"), radius, outline, fixed (never fades in a focus) edges color, width, dash ("dash", "dot"), arrow ("head", "both"), source (the edge it stands for), order (drawing order)

Edges are drawn from their first node to their second. Curves avoid nodes first and crossings second, and stay straight where that is clear.

docs.title: SVG and PDF
docs.text:
A Drawing writes itself as SVG text or as a one-page PDF, both as vector graphics. It is a COMPAS Data object as well, so it saves and loads as JSON.

with open("drawing.svg", "w") as f:
    f.write(drawing.to_svg())
drawing.to_pdf("drawing.pdf")

docs.title: graph_drawing.drawing
docs.text:
Drawings: a graph with positions, turned into plain primitives.

A drawing is a list of items in abstract units (y up), so the same picture can be rendered as Rhino geometry, on the Grasshopper canvas, as SVG and as PDF.

Items

{"t": "circle", "c": (x, y), "r": r, "fill": hex, "stroke": hex | None, "w": w}
{"t": "poly",   "pts": [...], "fill": hex | None, "stroke": hex | None, "w": w, "dash": None | "dash" | "dot"}
{"t": "line",   "pts": [...], "color": hex, "w": w, "dash": None | "dash" | "dot"}
{"t": "text",   "s": str, "pos": (x, y), "size": h, "color": hex,
                "anchor": "middle" | "start" | "end", "bold": bool}

Items of a node carry its key under "n", items of an edge the edge under "e", so a drawing can be recoloured for a focus without drawing it again.

Node attributes read by draw

label        text in the node (default: the key)
fill         fill colour (default grey)
stroke       ring colour, stroke_width its width
text_color   label colour (default: black or white, whichever reads better)
label_size   label height (default 0.19), bold (default True)
shape        "circle" (default), "octagon", "triangle" (pointing up) or "box"
radius       circle radius (default R), width and height for boxes
outline      radius where arrow tips end (default: the outer edge of the ring)
fixed        True: the node never fades in a focus (ground nodes)

Edge attributes read by draw

color        line colour, width its width
dash         None, "dash" or "dot"
arrow        "head" (arrow at the second node), "both" or None
source       the edge this one stands for, kept on its items under "e"
order        drawing order of the edges (default: the order of the graph)

def hex_rgb(h):
    """Red, green and blue of a hex colour.

    Parameters
    ----------
    h : str
        A colour such as ``"#3070b3"``.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[int, int, int]
        Each from 0 to 255.

    """
    h = h.lstrip("#")
    return int(h[0:2], 16), int(h[2:4], 16), int(h[4:6], 16)

def text_on(fill):
    """Black or white text, whichever reads better on the fill.

    Parameters
    ----------
    fill : str
        Hex colour of the background.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        Hex colour of the text.

    """
    r, g, b = [c / 255.0 for c in hex_rgb(fill)]
    lum = 0.2126 * r + 0.7152 * g + 0.0722 * b
    return "#ffffff" if lum < 0.45 else INK

def blend(h, f, to="#ffffff"):
    """A colour moved part of the way towards another.

    Parameters
    ----------
    h : str
        Hex colour.
    f : float
        Fraction of the way, from 0 (``h``) to 1 (``to``).
    to : str, optional
        Hex colour to move towards. Default white.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        Hex colour.

    """
    a, b = hex_rgb(h), hex_rgb(to)
    return "#%02x%02x%02x" % tuple(int(round(a[i] + (b[i] - a[i]) * f)) for i in range(3))

def arc(p, q, bow):
    """A quadratic arc from p to q, bulging sideways.

    Parameters
    ----------
    p : tuple[float, float]
        Start point.
    q : tuple[float, float]
        End point.
    bow : float
        Bulge as a fraction of the distance from p to q. 0 is straight, the sign picks the side.

    Returns
    -------
    list[tuple[float, float]]
        Points along the arc.

    """
    mx, my = (p[0] + q[0]) / 2.0, (p[1] + q[1]) / 2.0
    dx, dy = q[0] - p[0], q[1] - p[1]
    L = math.hypot(dx, dy) or 1.0
    nx, ny = -dy / L, dx / L
    c = (mx + nx * bow * L, my + ny * bow * L)
    return _qbez(p, c, q)

def route_edges(ends, pos, need):
    """Pick a bow per edge: straight when that is clear, otherwise the curve
    that avoids nodes first and other edges second, as gently as possible.

    Parameters
    ----------
    ends : list[tuple]
        The (a, b) node keys of every edge.
    pos : dict
        Position (x, y) per node key; every node is an obstacle.
    need : float
        Distance a curve should keep from the nodes it passes.

    Returns
    -------
    list[float]
        One bow per edge, for :func:`arc`.

    """
    pts = [pos[n] for n in pos]
    names = list(pos)

    def coarse(i, bw):
        a, b = ends[i]
        c = arc(pos[a], pos[b], bw)
        return c[::5] + ([c[-1]] if len(c) % 5 != 1 else [])

    def node_hits(i, poly):
        """Nodes the curve runs through (10 each) or close past (0.6 each)."""
        a, b = ends[i]
        x0, y0, x1, y1 = _bbox(poly)
        m = need + 0.3
        near = [p for n, p in zip(names, pts) if n not in (a, b)
                and x0 - m < p[0] < x1 + m and y0 - m < p[1] < y1 + m]
        score = 0.0
        for o in near:
            c = _clearance(poly, [o])
            score += 10.0 if c < need else (0.6 if c < m else 0.0)
        return score

    bows = [0.0] * len(ends)
    polys = [coarse(i, 0.0) for i in range(len(ends))]
    boxes = [_bbox(p) for p in polys]

    def cost(i, bw):
        poly = coarse(i, bw)
        box = _bbox(poly)
        cross = 0
        for j in range(len(ends)):
            if j == i:
                continue
            shared = set(ends[j]) & set(ends[i])
            if not shared:
                cross += _n_cross(poly, box, polys[j], boxes[j])
                continue
            # edges meeting at a node: only crossings away from that node count
            pa, pb = poly, polys[j]
            for n in shared:
                cut = R + 0.25
                pa = _cut_start(pa, cut) if ends[i][0] == n else _cut_end(pa, cut)
                pb = _cut_start(pb, cut) if ends[j][0] == n else _cut_end(pb, cut)
            if len(pa) > 1 and len(pb) > 1:
                cross += _n_cross(pa, _bbox(pa), pb, _bbox(pb))
        return node_hits(i, poly) + cross + 0.8 * abs(bw), poly, box

    # long edges first, they have the most room to swing out
    order = sorted(range(len(ends)), key=lambda i: -math.hypot(
        pos[ends[i][0]][0] - pos[ends[i][1]][0], pos[ends[i][0]][1] - pos[ends[i][1]][1]))
    for _ in range(8):
        changed = False
        for i in order:
            best = min((cost(i, bw) + (bw,) for bw in BOWS), key=lambda t: t[0])
            if best[3] != bows[i]:
                bows[i], polys[i], boxes[i] = best[3], best[1], best[2]
                changed = True
        if not changed:
            break
    return bows

    """Draw a graph whose nodes and edges carry the styling attributes.

    Parameters
    ----------

        The graph, with the node and edge attributes listed in the module docstring.
        Edges are drawn from their first to their second node.
    positions : dict
        Position (x, y) per node key. Nodes without a position are left out.
    regions : list[dict], optional
        Dashed boxes around groups of nodes: {"name": title, "nodes": [keys]},
        with an optional "side" (x, y) that places the title on the outer corner.
    title : str, optional
        Title in the upper left corner.
    legend : list[tuple[str, str]], optional
        (colour, text) entries in a row under the drawing.
    note : str, optional
        A line of explanation under the legend.
    route : bool, optional
        Curve edges around nodes and crossings (default True). False draws them straight.

    Returns
    -------
    :class:`Drawing`

    """
    pos = dict(positions)
    items = []
    data = {n: dict(graph.node[n]) for n in graph.nodes()}

    for region in regions or []:
        pts = [pos[n] for n in region["nodes"] if n in pos]
        if not pts:
            continue
        x0 = min(p[0] for p in pts) - R - 0.45
        x1 = max(p[0] for p in pts) + R + 0.45
        y0 = min(p[1] for p in pts) - R - 0.45
        y1 = max(p[1] for p in pts) + R + 0.45
        items.append({"t": "poly", "pts": [(x0, y0), (x1, y0), (x1, y1), (x0, y1)],
                      "fill": None, "stroke": INK_MUTED, "w": 0.025, "dash": "dash"})
        a = region.get("side") or (0.0, 0.0)
        tx = x1 - 0.2 if a[0] > 0.5 else x0 + 0.2
        ty = y1 + 0.35 if a[1] > -0.5 else y0 - 0.35
        items.append({"t": "text", "s": region["name"], "pos": (tx, ty), "size": 0.34,
                      "color": INK, "anchor": "end" if a[0] > 0.5 else "start", "bold": False})

    # edges, drawn under the nodes
    edges = []
    for (u, v), d in graph.edges(data=True):
        if u in pos and v in pos and u in data and v in data:
            edges.append((u, v, dict(d)))
    edges.sort(key=lambda e: e[2].get("order", 0))  # stable: without "order" the graph's own order
    if route:
        bows = route_edges([(u, v) for u, v, _ in edges], {n: pos[n] for n in pos if n in data}, R + 0.12)
    else:
        bows = [0.0] * len(edges)
    for (u, v, d), bow in zip(edges, bows):
        arrow = d.get("arrow")
        pts = _cut_to(arc(pos[u], pos[v], bow), _outline(data[u]), _outline(data[v]))
        source = d.get("source")
        for it in _edge_items(pts, d.get("color", INK), d.get("width", EDGE_W), d.get("dash"),
                              head=arrow in ("head", "both"), tail=arrow == "both"):
            it["e"] = tuple(source) if source is not None else (u, v)
            items.append(it)

    # nodes
    for n in pos:
        if n in data:
            items.extend(_node_items(n, pos[n][0], pos[n][1], data[n]))

    # legend under the drawing, title above it
    b0 = bounds(items) if items else (0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0)
    if legend:
        lx, ly = b0[0] + 0.3, b0[1] - 0.4
        x = lx
        for color, label in legend:
            items.append({"t": "circle", "c": (x + 0.15, ly), "r": 0.15, "fill": color, "stroke": None, "w": 0})
            items.append({"t": "text", "s": label, "pos": (x + 0.42, ly), "size": 0.22, "color": INK,
                          "anchor": "start", "bold": False})
            x += 0.42 + 0.13 * len(label) + 0.5
        if note:
            items.append({"t": "text", "s": note, "pos": (lx, ly - 0.5), "size": 0.19, "color": INK_MUTED,
                          "anchor": "start", "bold": False})
    elif note:
        items.append({"t": "text", "s": note, "pos": (b0[0] + 0.3, b0[1] - 0.4), "size": 0.19, "color": INK_MUTED,
                      "anchor": "start", "bold": False})
    if title:
        items.append({"t": "text", "s": title, "pos": (b0[0] + 0.3, b0[3] + 0.3), "size": 0.26,
                      "color": INK_MUTED, "anchor": "start", "bold": False})
    return Drawing(items, bounds(items), title)

def highlight(items, focus, colors=None):
    """The items with a focus on one node.

    Parameters
    ----------
    items : list[dict]
        The items of a drawing.
    focus : dict or None
        {"roles": {node: role}, "edges": set of frozenset node pairs}, with the
        role "sel" for the node in focus. None leaves the items as they are.
    colors : dict, optional
        Ring colour per role.

    Returns
    -------
    list[dict]
        The first len(items) entries correspond one to one to items (only
        colours change): nodes with a role and the edges of the focus keep
        their colours, everything else fades. Rings in the role colours follow.

    """
    if not focus:
        return list(items)
    colors = colors or {}
    roles, edges = focus["roles"], focus["edges"]
    out, rings = [], []
    for it in items:
        n, e = it.get("n"), it.get("e")
        if n is not None:
            if it.get("fixed") or n in roles:
                out.append(it)
                if it["t"] == "circle" and n in roles:
                    role = roles[n]
                    color = colors.get(role, INK)
                    if role == "sel":
                        rings.append(_ring(it["c"], it["r"] + 0.13, color, 0.08))
                    else:
                        rings.append(_ring(it["c"], it["r"] + 0.11, color, 0.05))
            else:
                out.append(_fade(it))
        elif e is not None:
            out.append(it if frozenset(e) in edges else _fade(it, 0.86))
        else:
            out.append(it)
    return out + rings

def pick(items, x, y, slack=0.08):
    """The node under a point of the drawing.

    Parameters
    ----------
    items : list[dict]
        The items of a drawing.
    x : float
        X of the point, in drawing units.
    y : float
        Y of the point, in drawing units.
    slack : float, optional
        How far outside a node a point still counts, in drawing units.

    Returns
    -------
    hashable | None
        The node key, or None if no node is there.

    """
    best = None
    for n, (cx, cy, r) in node_positions(items).items():
        d = math.hypot(x - cx, y - cy)
        if d <= r + slack and (best is None or d < best[0]):
            best = (d, n)
    return best[1] if best else None

def bounds(items):
    """The box around the items, with a small margin.

    Parameters
    ----------
    items : list[dict]
        The items of a drawing.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[float, float, float, float]
        ``(x0, y0, x1, y1)``.

    """
    xs, ys = [], []
    for it in items:
        if it["t"] == "circle":
            xs += [it["c"][0] - it["r"], it["c"][0] + it["r"]]
            ys += [it["c"][1] - it["r"], it["c"][1] + it["r"]]
        elif it["t"] == "text":
            x, y = it["pos"]
            w = 0.55 * it["size"] * len(it["s"])
            anchor = it.get("anchor", "middle")
            xs += [x, x + w] if anchor == "start" else ([x - w, x] if anchor == "end" else [x - w / 2, x + w / 2])
            ys += [y - it["size"], y + it["size"]]
        else:
            xs += [p[0] for p in it["pts"]]
            ys += [p[1] for p in it["pts"]]
    pad = 0.3
    return (min(xs) - pad, min(ys) - pad, max(xs) + pad, max(ys) + pad)

def to_svg(items, bnd, scale=60.0, font="Times New Roman"):
    """The items as SVG text.

    Parameters
    ----------
    items : list[dict]
        The items of a drawing.
    bnd : tuple[float, float, float, float]
        x0, y0, x1, y1 of the drawing.
    scale : float, optional
        Pixels per drawing unit.
    font : str, optional
        Font family of the text.

    Returns
    -------
    str

    """
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = bnd
    W, H = (x1 - x0) * scale, (y1 - y0) * scale

    def P(p):
        return "%.2f,%.2f" % ((p[0] - x0) * scale, (y1 - p[1]) * scale)

    out = ['<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="%.0f" height="%.0f" viewBox="0 0 %.2f %.2f">' % (W, H, W, H),
           '<rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="#ffffff"/>']
    for it in items:
        t = it["t"]
        if t == "circle":
            st = ' stroke="%s" stroke-width="%.2f"' % (it["stroke"], it["w"] * scale) if it.get("stroke") else ""
            cx, cy = P(it["c"]).split(",")
            out.append('<circle cx="%s" cy="%s" r="%.2f" fill="%s"%s/>' % (cx, cy, it["r"] * scale, it["fill"], st))
        elif t in ("poly", "line"):
            pts = " ".join(P(p) for p in it["pts"])
            if t == "poly":
                fill = it.get("fill") or "none"
                st = ' stroke="%s" stroke-width="%.2f"' % (it["stroke"], it["w"] * scale) if it.get("stroke") else ""
                da = _dash_array(it.get("dash"), it.get("w", 0.03), scale)
                if da:
                    st += ' stroke-dasharray="%.1f %.1f"' % tuple(da)
                out.append('<polygon points="%s" fill="%s"%s/>' % (pts, fill, st))
            else:
                da = _dash_array(it.get("dash"), it["w"], scale)
                st = ' stroke-dasharray="%.1f %.1f"' % tuple(da) if da else ""
                out.append('<polyline points="%s" fill="none" stroke="%s" stroke-width="%.2f" '
                           'stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"%s/>' % (pts, it["color"], it["w"] * scale, st))
        elif t == "text":
            x, y = P(it["pos"]).split(",")
            anchor = it.get("anchor", "middle")
            out.append('<text xml:space="preserve" x="%s" y="%s" font-family="%s" font-size="%.2f" fill="%s" text-anchor="%s" '
                       'dominant-baseline="central"%s>%s</text>'
                       % (x, y, font, it["size"] * scale * 1.35, it["color"], anchor,
                          ' font-weight="bold"' if it.get("bold") else "",
                          it["s"].replace("&", "&").replace("<", "<")))
    out.append("</svg>")
    return "\n".join(out)

def to_pdf(items, bnd, path, scale=28.0):
    """Write the items as a minimal one-page vector PDF.

    The text uses the standard fonts Times-Roman and Times-Bold, so nothing
    is embedded.

    Parameters
    ----------
    items : list[dict]
        The items of a drawing.
    bnd : tuple[float, float, float, float]
        x0, y0, x1, y1 of the drawing.
    path : str
        The file to write.
    scale : float, optional
        Points per drawing unit.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        The path.

    """
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = bnd
    W, H = (x1 - x0) * scale, (y1 - y0) * scale

    def P(p):
        return (p[0] - x0) * scale, (p[1] - y0) * scale

    ops = ["1 1 1 rg 0 0 %.2f %.2f re f" % (W, H), "1 J 1 j"]
    k = 0.5523
    for it in items:
        t = it["t"]
        if t == "circle":
            cx, cy = P(it["c"])
            r = it["r"] * scale
            path_ = ("%.2f %.2f m " % (cx + r, cy) +
                     "%.2f %.2f %.2f %.2f %.2f %.2f c " % (cx + r, cy + k * r, cx + k * r, cy + r, cx, cy + r) +
                     "%.2f %.2f %.2f %.2f %.2f %.2f c " % (cx - k * r, cy + r, cx - r, cy + k * r, cx - r, cy) +
                     "%.2f %.2f %.2f %.2f %.2f %.2f c " % (cx - r, cy - k * r, cx - k * r, cy - r, cx, cy - r) +
                     "%.2f %.2f %.2f %.2f %.2f %.2f c h" % (cx + k * r, cy - r, cx + r, cy - k * r, cx + r, cy))
            ops.append("%s rg %s f" % (_rgb(it["fill"]), path_))
            if it.get("stroke"):
                ops.append("[] 0 d %s RG %.2f w %s S" % (_rgb(it["stroke"]), it["w"] * scale, path_))
        elif t in ("poly", "line"):
            pts = [P(p) for p in it["pts"]]
            path_ = "%.2f %.2f m " % pts[0] + " ".join("%.2f %.2f l" % p for p in pts[1:])
            w = it.get("w", 0.03)
            da = _dash_array(it.get("dash"), w, scale)
            dash = "[%.1f %.1f] 0 d" % tuple(da) if da else "[] 0 d"
            if t == "poly":
                path_ += " h"
                if it.get("fill"):
                    ops.append("%s rg %s f" % (_rgb(it["fill"]), path_))
                if it.get("stroke"):
                    ops.append("%s %s RG %.2f w %s S" % (dash, _rgb(it["stroke"]), w * scale, path_))
            else:
                ops.append("%s %s RG %.2f w %s S" % (dash, _rgb(it["color"]), w * scale, path_))
        elif t == "text":
            x, y = P(it["pos"])
            size = it["size"] * scale * 1.35
            width = 0.5 * size * len(it["s"])  # Times-Roman average, good enough for codes
            anchor = it.get("anchor", "middle")
            x -= width / 2 if anchor == "middle" else (width if anchor == "end" else 0)
            s = it["s"].replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("(", "\\(").replace(")", "\\)")
            font = "/F2" if it.get("bold") else "/F1"
            ops.append("BT %s %.2f Tf %s rg %.2f %.2f Td (%s) Tj ET" % (font, size, _rgb(it["color"]), x, y - size * 0.33, s))
    content = "\n".join(ops).encode("latin-1", "replace")
    objs = [
        b"<< /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R >>",
        b"<< /Type /Pages /Kids [3 0 R] /Count 1 >>",
        ("<< /Type /Page /Parent 2 0 R /MediaBox [0 0 %.2f %.2f] /Contents 4 0 R "
         "/Resources << /Font << /F1 5 0 R /F2 6 0 R >> >> >>" % (W, H)).encode(),
        b"<< /Length %d >>\nstream\n" % len(content) + content + b"\nendstream",
        b"<< /Type /Font /Subtype /Type1 /BaseFont /Times-Roman >>",
        b"<< /Type /Font /Subtype /Type1 /BaseFont /Times-Bold >>",
    ]
    data = b"%PDF-1.4\n"
    offsets = []
    for i, o in enumerate(objs):
        offsets.append(len(data))
        data += b"%d 0 obj\n" % (i + 1) + o + b"\nendobj\n"
    xref = len(data)
    data += b"xref\n0 %d\n0000000000 65535 f \n" % (len(objs) + 1)
    for off in offsets:
        data += b"%010d 00000 n \n" % off
    data += b"trailer\n<< /Size %d /Root 1 0 R >>\nstartxref\n%d\n%%%%EOF\n" % (len(objs) + 1, xref)
    with open(path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(data)
    return path

Frames from JSON: parts as boxes, their contacts, which part carries which, and the support graph drawn after Bruun et al. 2024 (Construction Robotics 8:20, Fig. 7).

Conventions of the JSON (schema 2.1.0, a three.js scene, Y up)

origin      centre of the box
dimensions  width along local X, height along local Y, depth along local Z
rotation    Euler angles in radians, applied in three.js order "YXZ"
            (R = Ry * Rx * Rz). Checked against the corner model: with this
            order every listed connection touches, with "XYZ" the braces
            stand out of their wall plane.

build_graph     the contact graph: listed and geometric connections, support directions

def __init__(self, data, order=EULER_ORDER):
    self.data = data
    self.id = data["id"]
    self.label = data.get("label") or self.id
    self.status = (data.get("status") or "intact").lower()
    self.material = data.get("material") or ""
    self.notes = data.get("notes") or ""
    self.connections = list(data.get("connections") or [])
    self.type = member_type(self.id, self.label)
    o, d, r = data["origin"], data["dimensions"], data.get("rotation") or {}
    m = euler_matrix(r.get("x", 0.0), r.get("y", 0.0), r.get("z", 0.0), order)
    cols = [(m[0][i], m[1][i], m[2][i]) for i in range(3)]
    self.center = _yup_to_zup((o["x"], o["y"], o["z"]))
    self.axes = [_yup_to_zup(c) for c in cols]  # local X, Y, Z
    self.size = (d["width"], d["height"], d["depth"])
    self.half = tuple(0.5 * s for s in self.size)
    self.long = max(range(3), key=lambda i: self.size[i])
    self.code = self.id
    self.walls = []
    self.wall_u = {}
    self.wall_defs = []

def build_graph(parts, tol=CONTACT_TOL, geometric_edges=True):
    """Graph of the parts and their contacts.

    Parameters
    ----------
    parts : list[:class:`Part`]
        The parts, as from :func:`load_parts`.
    tol : float, optional
        Boxes closer than this (metres) count as touching.
    geometric_edges : bool, optional
        Also add face contacts the JSON does not list.

    Returns
    -------
    :class:`compas.datastructures.Graph`
        Node per part id with label, code, type, walls, wall_u, status, material,
        notes, center, size, fill (model colour), color (type colour), new.
        Edge attributes:

        * kind: "both" | "one-sided" | "geometric"
        * touching: True if the boxes touch within tol
        * gap: box gap in metres (negative = overlap)
        * contact: contact point (or None), contact_kind: "face" | "edge" | "point"
        * support: (supported, supporter), "both" or None

        Parts standing on the lowest level get an edge to the node "ground".
        Contacts only along an edge or a point stay out of the graph when the
        JSON does not list them (they are reported). The graph attributes hold
        unknown_connections, weak_contacts, contact_tol and walls.

    """
    g = Graph(name="contacts")
    byid = {p.id: p for p in parts}
    for p in parts:
        g.add_node(p.id, label=p.label, code=p.code, type=p.type, walls=list(p.walls), wall_u=dict(p.wall_u),
                   status=p.status, material=p.material, notes=p.notes, center=p.center,
                   size=p.size, fill=p.fill(), color=p.color, new=p.is_new)

    def add(a, b, kind):
        gap = box_gap(a, b)
        d = dict(kind=kind, gap=gap, touching=gap <= tol, contact=None,
                 contact_kind=None, support=None)
        if gap <= tol:
            c, ck = contact(a, b, tol)
            d.update(contact=c, contact_kind=ck, support=support_direction(a, b, c))
        g.add_edge(a.id, b.id, **d)

    unknown = []
    for p in parts:
        for q in p.connections:
            if q not in byid:
                unknown.append((p.id, q))
            elif q != p.id and not g.has_edge((p.id, q), directed=False):
                add(p, byid[q], "both" if p.id in byid[q].connections else "one-sided")

    weak = []
    if geometric_edges:
        for i, a in enumerate(parts):
            for b in parts[i + 1:]:
                if g.has_edge((a.id, b.id), directed=False) or box_gap(a, b) > tol:
                    continue
                c, ck = contact(a, b, tol)
                if ck == "face":
                    add(a, b, "geometric")
                else:
                    weak.append((a.id, b.id, ck))

    zmin = min(p.zmin() for p in parts) if parts else 0.0
    grounded = [p for p in parts if p.zmin() <= zmin + tol]
    if grounded:
        g.add_node(GROUND, label="Ground", code="G", type="ground", walls=[], wall_u={}, status="intact",
                   material="", notes="", center=(0, 0, zmin), size=(0, 0, 0),
                   fill="#000000", color="#000000", new=False)
        for p in grounded:
            g.add_edge(p.id, GROUND, kind="both", gap=0.0, touching=True,
                       contact=(p.center[0], p.center[1], zmin), contact_kind="face",
                       support=(p.id, GROUND))

    g.attributes.update(unknown_connections=unknown, weak_contacts=weak, contact_tol=tol,
                        walls=[{k: v for k, v in w.items() if k != "members"} for w in (parts[0].wall_defs if parts else [])])
    return g

def support_graph(g):
    """Directed graph of the support relations.

    Parameters
    ----------
    g : :class:`compas.datastructures.Graph`
        The contact graph of :func:`build_graph`.

    Returns
    -------
    :class:`compas.datastructures.Graph`
        An edge u -> v means u rests on v, the load path as in Bruun et al.
        Two parts that carry each other get edges in both directions.

    """
    d = Graph(name="support")
    for n in g.nodes():
        d.add_node(n, **dict(g.node[n]))
    for u, v, e in edges(g):
        s = e.get("support")
        if s == "both":
            d.add_edge(u, v, **dict(e))
            d.add_edge(v, u, **dict(e))
        elif s:
            d.add_edge(s[0], s[1], **dict(e))
    return d

def report(g):
    """A plain-text summary with the inconsistencies between JSON and geometry.

    Parameters
    ----------
    g : :class:`compas.datastructures.Graph`
        The contact graph of :func:`build_graph`.

    Returns
    -------
    str

    """
    parts = [n for n in g.nodes() if n != GROUND]
    all_edges = list(edges(g))
    lines = []
    kinds = {}
    for u, v, d in all_edges:
        if GROUND not in (u, v):
            kinds[d["kind"]] = kinds.get(d["kind"], 0) + 1
    lines.append("parts: %d   connections: %d   (%s)" % (
        len(parts), sum(kinds.values()), ", ".join("%s %d" % kv for kv in sorted(kinds.items()))))
    status = {}
    for n in parts:
        s = g.node[n]["status"]
        status[s] = status.get(s, 0) + 1
    lines.append("status: " + ", ".join("%s %d" % kv for kv in sorted(status.items())))
    new = [g.node[n]["code"] for n in parts if g.node[n].get("new")]
    if new:
        lines.append("new parts: " + ", ".join(new))
    if g.has_node(GROUND):
        lines.append("on the ground: " + ", ".join(g.node[n]["code"] for n in g.neighbors(GROUND)))

    def c(n):
        return "%s (%s)" % (g.node[n]["code"], n)

    iso = [n for n in parts if not any(edge_data(g, n, m)["kind"] != "geometric" for m in g.neighbors(n))]
    if iso:
        lines.append("no listed connection: " + ", ".join(c(n) for n in iso))
    one = [(u, v) for u, v, d in all_edges if d["kind"] == "one-sided"]
    if one:
        lines.append("listed by one side only: " + "; ".join("%s - %s" % (c(u), c(v)) for u, v in one))
    apart = [(u, v, d["gap"]) for u, v, d in all_edges
             if d["kind"] != "geometric" and not d["touching"]]
    if apart:
        lines.append("listed but not touching: " + "; ".join(
            "%s - %s (%.0f mm)" % (c(u), c(v), 1000 * gap) for u, v, gap in apart))
    geo = [(u, v) for u, v, d in all_edges if d["kind"] == "geometric"]
    if geo:
        lines.append("touching but not listed: " + "; ".join("%s - %s" % (c(u), c(v)) for u, v in geo))
    if g.attributes.get("weak_contacts"):
        lines.append("only edge or point contact, left out: " + "; ".join(
            "%s - %s" % (c(u), c(v)) for u, v, _ in g.attributes["weak_contacts"]))
    undirected = [(u, v) for u, v, d in all_edges if d.get("touching") and d.get("support") is None]
    if undirected:
        lines.append("no support direction found: " + "; ".join("%s - %s" % (c(u), c(v)) for u, v in undirected))
    if g.attributes.get("unknown_connections"):
        lines.append("unknown ids: " + "; ".join("%s -> %s" % tuple(e) for e in g.attributes["unknown_connections"]))
    return "\n".join(lines)

def drawing_graph(g):
    """The contact graph styled for :func:`graph_drawing.drawing.draw`.

    Every connection becomes an edge from the carried part to the carrying one
    (arrowheads at both ends where two parts carry each other), coloured like
    the carried part, solid when both parts list it, dashed when one does,
    dotted when neither does. The ground is drawn once per wall, like the
    foundation nodes in Bruun's figure: the node "ground:<wall>" stands for the
    ground under that wall. The keys of the original edges are kept under
    "source", so a focus on the contact graph can be shown on the drawing.

    Parameters
    ----------
    g : :class:`compas.datastructures.Graph`
        The contact graph of :func:`build_graph`.

    Returns
    -------
    :class:`compas.datastructures.Graph`
        Ready for :func:`graph_drawing.layouts.support` and :func:`graph_drawing.drawing.draw`.

    """
    dg = Graph(name="support drawing")
    walls = g.attributes.get("walls", [])
    dg.attributes["walls"] = walls
    for n in g.nodes():
        if n == GROUND:
            continue
        nd = g.node[n]
        fill = nd.get("color", "#7a7a75")
        status = nd.get("status")
        stroke, w, txt = None, 0.0, text_on(fill)
        if status == "missing":
            stroke, w, txt, fill = fill, 0.04, INK, MISSING_TAG
        if status == "defective":
            stroke, w = DEFECT, 0.09
        if nd.get("new"):
            stroke, w = INK, 0.06
        outline = R + 0.045 if status == "defective" else (R + 0.03 if nd.get("new") else R)
        dg.add_node(n, label=nd.get("code", n), fill=fill, stroke=stroke, stroke_width=w, text_color=txt,
                    outline=outline, type=nd.get("type"), walls=list(nd.get("walls", [])),
                    wall_u=dict(nd.get("wall_u", {})), center=nd.get("center"), status=status, new=nd.get("new"))
    single = set()
    for n in dg.nodes():
        ws = dg.node[n].get("walls", [])
        if len(ws) == 1:
            single.add(ws[0])
    for wall in walls:
        if wall["name"] in single:
            dg.add_node("%s:%s" % (GROUND, wall["name"]), label="", shape="triangle", fill="#000000",
                        ground=wall["name"], fixed=True)

    def wall_of(n):
        ws = g.node[n].get("walls", [])
        return ws[0] if ws else None

    for i, (u, v, d) in enumerate(edges(g)):
        s = d.get("support")
        a, b = (s[0], s[1]) if isinstance(s, (tuple, list)) else (u, v)
        if b == GROUND:
            b = "%s:%s" % (GROUND, wall_of(a))
        if a == GROUND:
            a = "%s:%s" % (GROUND, wall_of(b))
        if not (dg.has_node(a) and dg.has_node(b)):
            continue
        arrow = "both" if s == "both" else ("head" if s is not None else None)
        dg.add_edge(a, b, color=edge_color(g, u, v, d), dash={"one-sided": "dash", "geometric": "dot"}.get(d.get("kind")),
                    arrow=arrow, source=(u, v), order=i)
    return dg

def unsupported_without(g, sel):
    """Parts that lose all their support from below when sel is taken out.

    Fixpoint over the support relations: a part drops out when every part it
    rests on has dropped out. A part with another support left (a corner post
    that also stands on the other sill, a top beam that also rests on the
    other wall) stays. Mutual contacts (sills and top beams carrying each
    other at a corner) carry nothing here.
    Only gravity is read: rails held in the posts by tenons, or posts hanging
    from the top beam, count as unsupported all the same.

    Parameters
    ----------
    g : :class:`compas.datastructures.Graph`
        The contact graph of :func:`build_graph`.
    sel : str
        The part taken out.

    Returns
    -------
    list[str]
        In the order they drop out.

    """
    rests = {}
    for u, v, d in edges(g):
        s = d.get("support")
        if isinstance(s, (tuple, list)):
            rests.setdefault(s[0], set()).add(s[1])
    gone = [sel]
    out = {sel}
    changed = True
    while changed:
        changed = False
        for n, sup in rests.items():
            if n not in out and n != GROUND and sup and sup <= out:
                out.add(n)
                gone.append(n)
                changed = True
    return gone[1:]

def focus(g, sel, chain=False):
    """How every part relates to the selected one.

    Roles are the direct contacts: what the part rests on, what rests on it,
    what only touches it. "affected" are the parts that lose all support from
    below when it is taken out, see :func:`unsupported_without`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    g : :class:`compas.datastructures.Graph`
        The contact graph of :func:`build_graph`.
    sel : str
        The selected part.
    chain : bool, optional
        Also give the affected parts that are not direct contacts the role
        "above2", and keep their edges.

    Returns
    -------
    dict | None
        ``{"sel": id, "roles": {node: role}, "edges": set of node pairs,
        "affected": [ids], "chain": chain}``, or None if nothing is selected.

    """
    if sel is None or not g.has_node(sel):
        return None
    roles = {sel: "sel"}
    fedges = set()
    for v in g.neighbors(sel):
        s = edge_data(g, sel, v).get("support")
        if isinstance(s, (tuple, list)):
            role = "below" if s[0] == sel else "above"
        else:
            role = "touch"
        roles.setdefault(v, role)
        fedges.add(frozenset((sel, v)))
    affected = unsupported_without(g, sel)
    if chain:
        aset = set(affected) | {sel}
        for n in affected:
            roles.setdefault(n, "above2")
        for u, v, d in edges(g):
            s = d.get("support")
            if isinstance(s, (tuple, list)) and s[0] in aset and s[1] in aset:
                fedges.add(frozenset((u, v)))
    return {"sel": sel, "roles": roles, "edges": fedges, "affected": affected, "chain": chain}

    Returns
    -------
    list[tuple]
        ``(role or None, text)`` per line.

    """
    if not f:
        return []
    sel = f["sel"]
    d = g.node[sel]
    kind = TYPE.get(d.get("type"), TYPE["other"])["name"].lower()
    head = "%s  %s  (%s, %s%s)" % (d.get("code", sel), sel, kind, d.get("status", ""), ", new" if d.get("new") else "")
    lines = [("sel", head)]
    for role in ROLE_ORDER:
        ns = [n for n, r in f["roles"].items() if r == role]
        if role == "above2" and not ns:
            continue
        codes = sorted(g.node[n].get("code", n) for n in ns)
        lines.append((role, "%s: %s" % (ROLE_NAME[role], ", ".join(codes) if codes else "-")))
    if f["affected"]:
        codes = sorted(g.node[n].get("code", n) for n in f["affected"])
        lines.append((None,
                      "without support from below once it is out: " + ", ".join(codes)))
    notes = (d.get("notes") or "").strip()
    if notes:
        lines.append((None, "notes: " + (notes if len(notes) <= 90 else notes[:87] + "...")))
    return lines

def support(graph):
    """Positions in the manner of a plan seen from above, and the wall regions.

    Every wall gets a region on the side its outward normal points to (south
    wall below, west wall left, ...). Inside a region the members stand in
    columns by type, ground outside, and within a column in their order along
    the wall. Members of two walls stand in the corner between the two
    regions; members of no wall (joists, ...) in the middle.

    Parameters
    ----------
    graph : :class:`compas.datastructures.Graph`
        A graph as made by :func:`graph_drawing.frames.drawing_graph`: the
        graph attribute "walls" lists the walls (name, normal, along), every
        member node has "type", "walls", "wall_u" and "center", and one node
        per wall with the attribute "ground" (the wall's name) stands for the
        ground under it.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[dict, list[dict]]
        Position (x, y) per node, and one region per wall:
        {"name": "Front wall", "wall": name, "side": outward normal in the drawing, "nodes": [keys]}.

    """
    nodes = {n: graph.node[n] for n in graph.nodes()}
    walls = {w["name"]: w for w in graph.attributes.get("walls", [])}
    grounds = {d["ground"]: n for n, d in nodes.items() if d.get("ground")}
    parts = [n for n, d in nodes.items() if not d.get("ground")]
    single = {w: [n for n in parts if nodes[n].get("walls") == [w]] for w in walls}
    single = {w: ns for w, ns in single.items() if ns}
    corner = [n for n in parts if len(nodes[n].get("walls", [])) > 1]
    middle = [n for n in parts if not nodes[n].get("walls")]

    # columns per wall, inner offset large enough that neighbouring regions never touch
    cols, nbands = {}, {}
    for w, ns in single.items():
        # rails get one column per height level (lower rails nearer the posts), so
        # that every rail can stand above its own bay; top beams come after them
        zs = sorted(nodes[n]["center"][2] for n in ns if nodes[n].get("type") == "rail")
        bands = []
        for z in zs:
            if not bands or z - bands[-1][-1] > 0.25:
                bands.append([z])
            else:
                bands[-1].append(z)

        def band(z):
            return min(range(len(bands)), key=lambda i: abs(z - sum(bands[i]) / len(bands[i])))
        c = {}
        for n in ns:
            typ = nodes[n].get("type")
            if typ == "rail":
                ci = 3 + band(nodes[n]["center"][2])
            elif typ == "top":
                ci = 3 + len(bands)
            elif typ in ("sill", "post", "brace", "strut"):
                ci = _column_of(typ)
            else:
                ci = 4 + len(bands)
            c.setdefault(ci, []).append(n)
        cols[w] = c
        nbands[w] = len(bands)
    max_rows = max([len(ns) for c in cols.values() for ns in c.values()] + [1])
    inner = (max_rows - 1) / 2.0 * DY + R + 0.9 * DX
    if middle:
        inner = max(inner, (len(middle) - 1) / 2.0 * DY + R + 1.2 * DX)

    pos, regions = {}, []
    for w, c in cols.items():
        nb = nbands[w]
        nrm = walls[w]["normal"]
        a = (nrm[0], nrm[1])                  # outward, in the drawing
        t = (-a[1], a[0])                     # along the wall
        along = walls[w]["along"]
        used = sorted(c)
        sgn = along[0] * t[0] + along[1] * t[1]

        def key(n):
            return nodes[n]["wall_u"].get(w, 0.0) * sgn

        # reference column (posts if present): evenly spaced in wall order
        ref_ci = 2 if 2 in c else max(c, key=lambda ci: len(c[ci]))
        ref = sorted(c[ref_ci], key=lambda n: (key(n), -nodes[n]["center"][2]))
        ref_u = [key(n) for n in ref]
        ref_r = [(j - (len(ref) - 1) / 2.0) * DY for j in range(len(ref))]

        def interp(u):
            """Drawing coordinate of wall position u, between the reference members."""
            if len(ref_u) < 2 or ref_u[-1] - ref_u[0] < 1e-9:
                return 0.0
            if u <= ref_u[0]:
                return ref_r[0] + (u - ref_u[0]) / (ref_u[1] - ref_u[0] + 1e-9) * DY
            if u >= ref_u[-1]:
                return ref_r[-1] + (u - ref_u[-1]) / (ref_u[-1] - ref_u[-2] + 1e-9) * DY
            for i in range(1, len(ref_u)):
                if u <= ref_u[i]:
                    f = (u - ref_u[i - 1]) / (ref_u[i] - ref_u[i - 1] + 1e-9)
                    return ref_r[i - 1] + f * (ref_r[i] - ref_r[i - 1])
            return ref_r[-1]

        for k, ci in enumerate(reversed(used)):  # innermost column first
            ns = sorted(c[ci], key=lambda n: (key(n), -nodes[n]["center"][2]))
            if ci == ref_ci:
                rs = list(ref_r)
            else:
                # each member sits where it is along the wall, relative to the posts,
                # pushed apart just enough that nodes do not overlap
                want = [interp(key(n)) for n in ns]
                rs = []
                for x in want:
                    rs.append(x if not rs else max(x, rs[-1] + GAP))
                shift = (sum(want) - sum(rs)) / len(rs)
                rs = [r + shift for r in rs]
                for i in range(len(rs) - 2, -1, -1):  # keep the gap after the shift
                    rs[i] = min(rs[i], rs[i + 1] - GAP)
            if ci > 3 and ci < 3 + nb:  # upper rail bands slightly staggered,
                rs = [r + 0.22 * DY * ((ci - 3) % 2) for r in rs]  # so their edges do not run over the lower rails
            dist = inner + k * DX
            for n, r in zip(ns, rs):
                pos[n] = (a[0] * dist + t[0] * r, a[1] * dist + t[1] * r)
        g = grounds.get(w)
        region = list(single[w])
        if g is not None:
            dist = inner + len(used) * DX
            pos[g] = (a[0] * dist, a[1] * dist)
            region.append(g)
        regions.append({"name": "%s wall" % w.capitalize(), "wall": w, "side": a, "nodes": region})

    # corners: between the two regions they belong to
    groups = {}
    for n in corner:
        groups.setdefault(tuple(sorted(nodes[n]["walls"])), []).append(n)
    for key, ns in groups.items():
        dirs = [walls[w]["normal"] for w in key if w in walls]
        cx = sum(d[0] for d in dirs)
        cy = sum(d[1] for d in dirs)
        L = math.hypot(cx, cy) or 1.0
        cx, cy = cx / L, cy / L
        dist = inner * math.sqrt(2.0) * 0.85
        tx, ty = -cy, cx
        ns.sort(key=lambda n: -nodes[n]["center"][2])
        for j, n in enumerate(ns):
            r = (j - (len(ns) - 1) / 2.0) * DY
            pos[n] = (cx * dist + tx * r, cy * dist + ty * r)

    # middle: members of no wall, spread along their main direction in plan
    if middle:
        xs = [nodes[n]["center"][0] for n in middle]
        ys = [nodes[n]["center"][1] for n in middle]
        horiz = (max(xs) - min(xs)) >= (max(ys) - min(ys))
        middle.sort(key=lambda n: nodes[n]["center"][0] if horiz else nodes[n]["center"][1])
        for j, n in enumerate(middle):
            r = (j - (len(middle) - 1) / 2.0) * DY * 1.4
            pos[n] = (r, 0.0) if horiz else (0.0, r)
    return pos, regions

def layers(graph):
    """Layer of every node: the length of the longest path of edges ending in it.

    Edges that close a cycle are left out (the first edge found that leads
    back to a node on the current path), so the result is defined for any
    directed graph.

    Parameters
    ----------
    graph : :class:`compas.datastructures.Graph`
        A directed graph.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        Layer index per node key, starting at 0.

    """
    keys = list(graph.nodes())
    out = {n: [] for n in keys}
    for (u, v) in graph.edges():
        if u != v:
            out[u].append(v)
    # depth first: drop edges back onto the current path
    state, keep = {}, {n: [] for n in keys}
    for root in keys:
        if root in state:
            continue
        stack = [(root, iter(out[root]))]
        state[root] = 1
        while stack:
            n, it = stack[-1]
            for m in it:
                if state.get(m) == 1:
                    continue  # back edge
                keep[n].append(m)
                if m not in state:
                    state[m] = 1
                    stack.append((m, iter(out[m])))
                break
            else:
                state[n] = 2
                stack.pop()
    indeg = {n: 0 for n in keys}
    for n in keys:
        for m in keep[n]:
            indeg[m] += 1
    layer = {n: 0 for n in keys}
    ready = [n for n in keys if indeg[n] == 0]
    while ready:
        n = ready.pop(0)
        for m in keep[n]:
            layer[m] = max(layer[m], layer[n] + 1)
            indeg[m] -= 1
            if indeg[m] == 0:
                ready.append(m)
    return layer

def layered(graph, direction="down", spacing=0.6, gap=0.35, sweeps=4):
    """Positions for a directed graph in layers along its edges.

    Parameters
    ----------
    graph : :class:`compas.datastructures.Graph`
        The graph. Edges point from earlier to later steps.
    direction : {"down", "right"}, optional
        Where the edges point: "down" puts the first layer on top,
        "right" puts it on the left.
    spacing : float, optional
        Free space between two layers.
    gap : float, optional
        Free space between two nodes of a layer.
    sweeps : int, optional
        Rounds of reordering within the layers (barycentres of the neighbours).

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[dict, list]
        Position (x, y) per node and an empty list of regions.

    """
    from .drawing import _box_size

    layer = layers(graph)
    rows = {}
    for n in graph.nodes():  # insertion order is the first order within a layer
        rows.setdefault(layer[n], []).append(n)
    order = [rows[i] for i in sorted(rows)]
    preds = {n: [] for n in graph.nodes()}
    succs = {n: [] for n in graph.nodes()}
    for (u, v) in graph.edges():
        preds[v].append(u)
        succs[u].append(v)

    def size(n):
        """Extent of a node across its layer and along the direction."""
        d = graph.node[n]
        if d.get("shape") == "box":
            w, h = _box_size(d)
        else:
            w = h = 2 * d.get("radius", R)
        return (w, h) if direction == "down" else (h, w)

    def place(row):
        """Coordinates across the layer, centred on 0."""
        widths = [size(n)[0] for n in row]
        total = sum(widths) + gap * (len(row) - 1)
        x, out = -total / 2.0, {}
        for n, w in zip(row, widths):
            out[n] = x + w / 2.0
            x += w + gap
        return out

    for s in range(sweeps):
        down = s % 2 == 0
        idx = range(1, len(order)) if down else range(len(order) - 2, -1, -1)
        for i in idx:
            ref = place(order[i - 1] if down else order[i + 1])
            cur = place(order[i])

            def bary(n):
                nbrs = [m for m in (preds[n] if down else succs[n]) if m in ref]
                return sum(ref[m] for m in nbrs) / len(nbrs) if nbrs else cur[n]
            order[i] = sorted(order[i], key=lambda n: (bary(n), cur[n]))

    pos = {}
    along, prev = 0.0, None
    for row in order:
        depth = max(size(n)[1] for n in row)
        if prev is not None:
            along += (prev + depth) / 2.0 + spacing
        prev = depth
        across = place(row)
        for n in row:
            pos[n] = (across[n], -along) if direction == "down" else (along, -across[n])
    return pos, []

def from_model(model):
    """A styled graph of a compas_model model and its state.

    Parameters
    ----------
    model : :class:`compas_model.models.Model`
        The model. Its graph carries the attributes listed in the module docstring.

    Returns
    -------
    :class:`compas.datastructures.Graph`
        One box per element, labelled with its name and coloured by type; red
        for damaged elements, a black ring for new ones, yellow for
        missing ones, white with a dashed outline for elements taken out.
        Connections with a support direction point from the carried element
        to the carrying one; released connections are dashed, open ones
        dotted. Grounded elements point to one ground node, a black triangle.

    """
    G = model.graph
    g = Graph(name=model.name or "model")
    name = {}
    grounded = []
    types = []
    for node in G.nodes():
        t = G.node[node].get("type") or "other"
        if t not in types:
            types.append(t)
    colors = _type_colors(types)
    for node in G.nodes():
        element = G.node_element(node)
        key = element.name if element is not None else str(node)
        name[node] = key
        d = G.node[node]
        style = _style(d, colors[d.get("type") or "other"])
        g.add_node(key, label=key, shape="box", bold=False, type=d.get("type") or "other", type_color=colors[d.get("type") or "other"],
                   fabric=d.get("fabric", "original"), condition=d.get("condition", "sound"),
                   placement=d.get("placement", "in"), **style)
        if d.get("grounded"):
            grounded.append(key)
    for i, (u, v) in enumerate(G.edges()):
        d = G.edge[u][v]
        a, b = name[u], name[v]
        s = d.get("support")
        arrow = None
        if isinstance(s, (list, tuple)) and len(s) == 2:
            a, b = s[0], s[1]
            arrow = "head"
        elif s == "both":
            arrow = "both"
        color = g.node[a].get("type_color", INK_MUTED) if arrow == "head" else INK_MUTED
        dash = {"released": "dash", "open": "dot"}.get(d.get("state"))
        g.add_edge(a, b, color=color, dash=dash, arrow=arrow, source=(name[u], name[v]), order=i,
                   joint=d.get("joint"), state=d.get("state", "secured"))
    if grounded:
        g.add_node(GROUND, label="", shape="triangle", fill="#000000", fixed=True)
        for k in grounded:
            g.add_edge(k, GROUND, color=g.node[k]["type_color"], arrow="head",
                       source=(k, GROUND), order=len(name) + len(grounded))
    return g

def drawing(model, title=None, direction="down", positions=None):
    """Draw a compas_model model with :func:`from_model`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    model : :class:`compas_model.models.Model`
        The model.
    title : str, optional
        Title of the drawing. Defaults to the model's name.
    direction : {"down", "right"}, optional
        Direction of the support arrows in the layered layout.
    positions : dict, optional
        Position (x, y) per element name, for example where the members are
        in the structure. The ground node goes below the grounded elements.
        Without positions, the layered layout places the elements.

    Returns
    -------
    :class:`graph_drawing.drawing.Drawing`

    """
    g = from_model(model)
    if positions:
        pos, regions = dict(positions), []
        if g.has_node(GROUND) and GROUND not in pos:
            below = [pos[n] for n in g.neighbors(GROUND) if n in pos] or list(pos.values())
            pos[GROUND] = (sum(p[0] for p in below) / len(below), min(p[1] for p in pos.values()) - 1.0)
    else:
        pos, regions = layouts.layered(g, direction=direction)
    entries = []
    for n in g.nodes():
        d = g.node[n]
        if n != GROUND and (d["type_color"], d["type"]) not in entries:
            entries.append((d["type_color"], d["type"]))
    note = ("arrow: rests on    black triangle: ground    red: damaged    black ring: new    yellow: missing    "
            "white: taken out    dashed: released    dotted: open")
    return draw(g, pos, regions, title=title or model.name, legend=entries, note=note)

def steps(labels, edges=None, fills=None):
    """A graph of labelled steps, ready for :func:`graph_drawing.layouts.layered`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    labels : list[str] or dict
        The label of every step, as a list (keys 0, 1, 2, ...) or as a dict {key: label}.
    edges : list[tuple], optional
        (before, after) pairs of keys. Defaults to a chain in the given order.
    fills : dict, optional
        Fill colour per key (default white).

    Returns
    -------
    :class:`compas.datastructures.Graph`

    Examples
    --------
    >>> from graph_drawing import steps, layouts, draw
    >>> g = steps(["Release pegs", "Withdraw post", "Insert new post", "Secure"])
    >>> pos, regions = layouts.layered(g)
    >>> d = draw(g, pos, regions)

    """
    if not isinstance(labels, dict):
        labels = dict(enumerate(labels))
    keys = list(labels)
    if edges is None:
        edges = list(zip(keys, keys[1:]))
    fills = fills or {}
    g = Graph(name="steps")
    for k in keys:
        g.add_node(k, label=str(labels[k]), shape="box", fill=fills.get(k, "#ffffff"), stroke=INK,
                   stroke_width=0.025, text_color=INK, bold=False)
    for i, (u, v) in enumerate(edges):
        g.add_edge(u, v, color=INK_MUTED, arrow="head", order=i)
    return g

def draw(self, items, z0=0.0, first=0):
    """Add the geometry of the items. Returns the height of the last item."""
    z = z0
    for i, it in enumerate(items):
        i += first
        z += 0.0002  # later items slightly above earlier ones
        t = it["t"]
        if t == "circle":
            c, r = it["c"], it["r"]
            ring = [(c[0] + r * math.cos(2 * math.pi * k / 48), c[1] + r * math.sin(2 * math.pi * k / 48))
                    for k in range(48)]
            self._src = (i, "fill")
            self.fan(ring, it["fill"], z)
            if it.get("stroke"):
                self._src = (i, "stroke")
                self.ribbon(ring, it["w"], it["stroke"], z + 0.0002, closed=True)
        elif t == "poly":
            if it.get("fill"):
                self._src = (i, "fill")
                self.fan(it["pts"], it["fill"], z)
            if it.get("stroke"):
                self._src = (i, "stroke")
                pts = list(it["pts"]) + [it["pts"][0]]
                for piece in dash_pieces(pts, it.get("dash")):
                    self.ribbon(piece, it["w"], it["stroke"], z)
        elif t == "line":
            self._src = (i, "color")
            for piece in dash_pieces(it["pts"], it.get("dash")):
                self.ribbon(piece, it["w"], it["color"], z)
        elif t == "text":
            self._src = (i, "color")
            self.text(it["s"], it["pos"], it["size"], it["color"], it.get("anchor", "middle"), z + 0.001)
    return z

def dash_pieces(pts, dash):
    """Split a polyline into the pieces of a dashed or dotted line.

    Parameters
    ----------
    pts : list[tuple[float, float]]
        The polyline, in drawing units.
    dash : str | None
        "dash", "dot", or None for a solid line.

    Returns
    -------
    list[list[tuple[float, float]]]
        The visible pieces.

    """
    if not dash:
        return [pts]
    on_len, off_len = (0.18, 0.10) if dash == "dash" else (0.04, 0.09)
    pieces, cur, on, left = [], [pts[0]], True, on_len
    for (x0, y0), (x1, y1) in zip(pts, pts[1:]):
        seg = math.hypot(x1 - x0, y1 - y0)
        t0 = 0.0
        while seg - t0 > left:
            t0 += left
            q = (x0 + (x1 - x0) * t0 / seg, y0 + (y1 - y0) * t0 / seg)
            if on:
                cur.append(q)
                pieces.append(cur)
            cur = [q]
            on = not on
            left = on_len if on else off_len
        left -= seg - t0
        if on:
            cur.append((x1, y1))
    if on and len(cur) > 1:
        pieces.append(cur)
    return pieces

def to_rhino(drawing, plane=None, unit=1.0, origin_at_corner=True):
    """A drawing as Rhino geometry and colours.

    Parameters
    ----------
    drawing : :class:`graph_drawing.drawing.Drawing`
        The drawing.
    plane : :rhino:`Rhino.Geometry.Plane`, optional
        The plane to draw on (default: World XY).
    unit : float, optional
        Size of one drawing unit in document units.
    origin_at_corner : bool, optional
        Put the lower left corner of the drawing at the plane's origin (default True).

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[list, list]
        The geometry and one System.Drawing.Color per piece.

    """
    plane = rg.Plane(plane) if plane is not None else rg.Plane.WorldXY
    if origin_at_corner:
        x0, y0 = drawing.bounds[0], drawing.bounds[1]
        plane.Origin = plane.PointAt(-x0 * unit, -y0 * unit)
    rd = RhinoDrawing(plane, unit)
    rd.draw(drawing.items)
    return rd.geo, rd.col
